_note: Runs BEFORE lib/director.md Stage 1. director.md assumes character sheets already exist. This is how the guide makes them. The realism of the reference sets the ceiling on the realism of every clip.

part_a.what: The starting portrait. Everything else is built on it.
part_a.model: Nano Banana 2 or GPT Image 2. For vintage tones use GPT Image 2 - it is the only model that holds analog film tone.
part_a.aspect: 3:4 for Modern/Digital-IMAX. 16:9 for vintage tones (film is widescreen, so the training data matches).

routes.existing_photo: Have a real photo? Clean it up as the starting reference. Face clearly visible, sharp, forward-facing, high resolution.
routes.describe: No photo? Use the Part A portrait prompt in guide/blueprint-extract.txt and describe the face and outfit.

reject_if: looks like a render not a photograph
skin too smooth, no pores or imperfections
flat lighting with no natural depth
hair reads as a solid mass not strands
eyes lack iris detail or a catchlight
part_a.note: If it looks too smooth, too perfect, or too digital, regenerate. Everything downstream inherits this.

part_b.prompt: Create a side view of the person.
part_b.check: Same face, same hair, same grain and colour treatment as Part A. If tone fidelity drops, regenerate.

part_c.model: Nano Banana 2 - EXCEPT the A24 tone, which needs GPT Image 2. Nano Banana renders A24 technically clean but loses the muted palette and soft grain.
part_c.outfit_reference: Best on a clean white background with nobody wearing it. If it is worn, crop the head out first.
part_c.panels: Top left front face close-up, bottom left side face close-up, right tall panel full body in the outfit. Not three-quarter.
check: identical character across all three panels
original face lighting preserved, not flattened
faces cropped tight with no remnant of the original outfit

era_matching.rule: The character must belong to the era of the chosen visual tone.
era_matching.why: The models were trained on real films. A modern face, modern hair and modern styling dropped into an 80s tone is a contradiction the model cannot resolve cleanly.
era_matching.also: Cultural fit counts too, not only period.

character_sheet.from_behind: Never pass a face sheet on a from-behind shot. The model satisfies both constraints by rendering the face on a duplicate second person. Let wardrobe carry identity instead.

product_sheet.when: Any physical product on screen - bottle, device, box, packaging.
skip_when: software, app, SaaS, website - use a clean UI screenshot instead
you already have a clean real photo of the product - use it directly as the @
product_sheet.check: Colours, labels and materials match the real product. Regenerate if anything is off.

location.rule: The location is NEVER a user question and never a written description at this stage. It is produced by director.md Stage 2 as base image, then wide shot, then location sheet - in that order, each from the previous one.
